items.summary: Two major ongoing infrastructure incidents on June 3 morning. First: the Longview Nippon Dynawave paper mill CSB investigation advances to Day 9. All 11 victims of the May 26 chemical tank implosion have been recovered and identified. Approximately 90,000 gallons of white liquor remain inside the structurally unstable tank. Columbia River contamination assessment is ongoing; EPA Region 10 and WA Department of Ecology monitoring active; Longview wellhead remains on diversion; drinking water confirmed safe. The pre-warning regulatory thread — March 2026 workers notified WA DOLI of a sinkhole at the implosion site — defines the investigation's regulatory liability arc. CSB investigation is in early-stage documentation and evidence preservation; no preliminary findings published. Second: the Sound Transit $34.5B funding gap overhaul (board vote June 2) is confirmed from yesterday's board action. The Ballard Link Extension from Seattle Center to Market Street is 'not currently affordable' and requires additional funding before construction can proceed. The initial Ballard Link segment to Seattle Center remains funded; West Seattle Link continues (Avalon Station removed); Tacoma and West Seattle extensions proceed. Revenue measures under review: fare gates, Washington Clean Fuels Standard carbon credit program, other operational changes. The additional funding mechanism for the Market Street extension is unresolved in both timeline and yield. Sound Transit's ORCA 3-Day Puget Pass launched June 1 as a rider retention and summer access measure. The $34.5B gap represents one of the largest unfunded regional transit obligations in the western United States and fundamentally reshapes the ST3 expansion voters approved in 2016.

items.summary: The local PNW fire picture on June 3 morning: NIFC above-normal fire potential designation for east of the Cascade Crest enters Day 3 with no new major ignitions overnight. Oregon fire season active Day 27. BLM full OR/WA campfire restrictions Day 21. Level 1 Central Oregon restrictions (Deschutes, Ochoco, Crooked River) Day 17. Bureau of Reclamation water rationing for Central Washington irrigators Day 14. East of the Cascades, conditions are advancing through the key early-June curing period: live fuels in rangeland areas are beginning to cure; dead fuels are drying. The NIFC east-side rangeland assessment explicitly forecasts above-normal significant fire potential rising materially through June before the July major-onset window. West of the Cascades, green-up continues to provide normal-risk moderation; this deteriorates rapidly during warm periods and does not hold through summer. The 2018 analog holds — July is the projected month of largest increase in significant fire activity — with the 2015 extreme trajectory remaining possible. Fire crew labor crunch is now active: green card policy reversal labor intersection is this week, simultaneous with NIFC above-normal Day 3 and Oregon Fire Day 27. Forest Service research station cuts (April 2026) reduce early-warning capacity entering the highest-risk period. Drought baseline unchanged: 82% Oregon drought coverage, Southern Cascades at extreme, fourth consecutive Washington drought emergency, snowpack one-third of normal. AccuWeather 2026 national forecast projects 5.5 to 8 million acres burned; Oregon's fire season forecast to last into October.

WA DOH update expected; Kittitas County active; Snohomish County 14+; Oregon OHA stale 40+ days. Fifth: Oregon gas at record $5.35/gallon; Washington approximately $5.78. Pump relief timeline conditionally intact per Iran comms resolving signal but contingent on MOU signing plus 30-day mine-removal; late July at earliest.

analyst_summary: June 3, 2026 Morning — Hormuz Day 96, Naval Blockade Day 53, Project Freedom Pause Day 29, WPA Day 95 Day 5 Past Hard Constitutional Deadline, Warsh Day 20, Acting DNI Day 13. Vibe 3: firmer floor than June 2 morning's lower-edge characterization. The June 3 morning opening is defined by two overnight constructive signals that shift the Iran risk posture from acute-ambiguity to resolving-ambiguity. First: the Iran comms suspension (Iranian state media June 1, attributed to Israeli Lebanon strikes) is showing resolution signals — a CNN regional source reported talks were back on track hours after the June 1 announcement; Secretary Rubio stated on June 2 that Khamenei 'appears more active' as talks continue, the most substantive constructive Khamenei engagement signal since the May 26 broad-principles endorsement. Two independent sourcing lines point toward comms restoration. CENTCOM self-defense operative; no repositioning or kinetic resumption; dual-principal approval gap advances to Day 6. Rubio also separately clarified nuclear sequencing: Iran must negotiate 'severe and long-term' limits; technical talks could take months — framing the MOU as a war-ending/Hormuz document with nuclear architecture to follow, consistent with established framework. Brent tracking near the $95 area at morning open. Second: the June 2–3 Washington Israel-Lebanon talks (fourth round) enter their final session today. Day 1 produced a partial ceasefire — Beirut-suburbs truce (Israel commits not to strike Dahiyeh; Hezbollah commits not to attack Israel) as a step toward full Lebanon-wide framework. Today's conclusion is the primary diplomatic watch window; Lebanon and Iran deal tracks remain operationally linked. New economic framing signal emerged: Marketplace June 2 surfaced that Warsh at his April confirmation hearing said he prefers 'trimmed averages' — April trimmed mean PCE came in at 2.3%, well below headline CPI (3.8%) and PCE (3.3%); if this is Warsh's operative framework, he may have materially more policy latitude at the June 16–17 inaugural FOMC than headline inflation implies. Structural stresses unchanged: WPA Day 95 (Day 5 past hard deadline, no enforcement), Reconciliation 2.0 stuck on anti-weaponization fund (July 4 pressure, week of June 8 floor window), NIFC above-normal Day 3 (east-side drying advancing, July onset unchanged, fire crew labor crunch active), measles ~2,013+ (2,000 crossed, CIDRAP slowing, school window 4 days, new King County transit-linked infant case on 2-Line), FEMA hurricane season Day 3 degraded, Longview CSB Day 9 (90,000 gallons unstable tank), Sound Transit $34.5B confirmed (Ballard-Market Street funding unresolved), Portland Council amendments today (T-28), gas records, green card labor crunch active. US Infrastructure Development Conference opens today in Dallas (Day 1 of 2). Vibe 3 firmer floor — two genuine constructive inputs; upgrade to 4 requires formal MOU endorsement from either principal or substantive Lebanon framework output today.
